rows.summary: "did" is weak only as a main verb: Auto-Fix leaves "did not" and "did never" as written (no more "Delivered not miss"), the optimizer no longer flags them, and "Did the audit" still becomes "Delivered the audit".
The ATS score counts a weak phrase only as whole words: "Networked with", "unhandled" and "Reworked" are no longer passive language; "Worked with" and "handled" still are.

statementRange reads the paragraph or item as a flat run of text and line breaks through inline wrappers, so a
inside bold or a link splits lines (

A
B

opens on the caret's line and Apply replaces only it), a caret at any element boundary finds the line beside it, and a list item holding a nested list opens on its own line; before this, it opened with the sub-items' text and Apply wiped them.

A power verb put before a first word that is no verb lowercases it only when the word is never a name (an article, preposition, pronoun, determiner, conjunction or helper verb): "Kubernetes cluster", "New Relic" and "I led" keep their capital, and "In 2023" and "The checkout" become lowercase. Product call: an ordinary capitalised noun ("Customer onboarding") now keeps its capital too, since no word list can tell it from a name and lowercasing a name is the worse mistake.

A metric chip after a statement ending in an abbreviation (etc., Inc., Ltd., Co., Jr., vs., U.S., e.g.) keeps the abbreviation's dot and still ends the sentence: "…SDKs, etc. by 35%.". A unit or ordinal ("200 ms.", "1st.") is treated as an ordinary sentence end.

hasMetric (the optimizer's and the ATS score's single metric rule) treats every digit glued to letters as part of a name, not only the first one, and reads a fiscal year in any spelling (FY2021, FY21-22, FY 21, FY-21, FY'21) as a date. "FY2021" and "v2.0" no longer count as metrics; "x10", "Rs.500", "EUR500k", "INR5,00,000", "3.5x" and "$1.2M" still do.

extractBulletsFromItem keeps track of the open item at each list depth, so text after a nested list continues the outer bullet the PDF prints it under ("Led migration for 3 regions"), and a nested item's continuation paragraph stays with that nested item. Checked at three depths.

issues: R4-LO-15: the first rule was too broad ("x10", "Rs.500", "EUR500k" stopped counting) and missed "FY2021-22" / "FY 21"; reworked in c649753.
R4-LO-14: "200 ms." and "1st." were read as abbreviations; fixed in 8da703d.
R4-LO-13: "I led" became "i led", and "New"/"First" were lowercased before a name ("New Relic"); fixed in f00455a, along with the stale JSDoc.
R4-LO-12: a caret at an element boundary (the edge of a wrapper, or just before a nested list) gave no statement; fixed in a5997d9 by mapping the boundary onto the flat leaf list.
R4-LO-10: "did never" was still rewritten; fixed in 9a20764.
